text:
alex.h: hey team — new hire here. Trying to get Vault/KMS access for my first-week tasks. what steps do I need to follow?

maria.s: welcome! :wave: short answer: request access via the secrets-bot, attach justification and duration, then infra will approve and grant a role with short-lived creds. longer version below.

jon.d: tagging a couple of useful notes from onboarding: 1) never store plaintext secrets in repo, 2) prefer KMS-wrapped secrets for long-lived artifacts, 3) use role-based access for apps not users.

alex.h: thanks — what's the exact command or request format for the secrets-bot?

secrets-bot: To request Vault user access open a thread to @secrets-bot with the following fields: `env`, `resource`, `reason`, `duration_hours`. Example message: `@secrets-bot request env=staging resource=api/stripe reason="onboarding integration testing" duration_hours=8` 

sam.k: if you need service account keys for CI, file a request and include the repo name + pipeline job. We issue ephemeral keys and store them in the pipeline secret store for you.

alex.h: ok — I need access to `secret/data/team/redwood-inference/stripe` for a quick integration run (2 hours). Sending request now.

alex.h: @secrets-bot request env=staging resource=secret/data/team/redwood-inference/stripe reason="testing stripe webhook integration" duration_hours=2

secrets-bot: Request received. Ticket #SEC-5321 created. Please allow ~30m for approval. If this is urgent, ping @maria.s or @sam.k with the ticket number.

maria.s: approving now for testing window. A couple of rotation notes: we rotate KMS-wrapped service keys monthly, user access tokens every 8 hours by default. If you need longer-term secrets for a service, ask for a service-role and we'll set automatic rotation.

jon.d: quick ops tips: to read a secret locally use the Vault CLI once your session is granted: ``vault kv get -field=value secret/team/redwood-inference/stripe``. For ephemeral creds we expose them as env vars in the runner: `REDSHIFT_API_KEY` style.

alex.h: got the creds and can read the secret, thanks! any docs I should skim so I don't accidentally request too many privileges?

maria.s: yep — start with internal guide: https://redwood.internal/security/secrets-onboarding (section "Quick start for new hires"). Also follow the checklist in the ticket: least privilege, short duration, rotate if used in CI, and add the ticket ID to PR descriptions when a secret is referenced.

sam.k: extra: if you need KMS wrapping (we wrap secrets for cross-account sharing), include `wrap=true` and the target account in the request. That triggers an additional approval from cloud-security.

alex.h: super helpful — one follow-up: who can approve production secret access?

maria.s: production access requires 2 approvers: one from eng-security and one from the owning product/infra team. We'll flag prod requests for an audit and require justification plus a runbook for revocation.

alex.h: perfect. thanks everyone, closing the loop here once integration tests finish. :thumbsup:

maria.s: welcome aboard! ping in #eng-security if anything else pops up.
